ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing and continuous screening against the Spanish SEBLAC/SEPBLAC lists, Ministry of the Interior and Ministry of Justice terrorist designations, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, OFAC's SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, and domestic PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for any politically exposed person, direct or indirect beneficial owner residing outside Spain, or corporate shareholder from a FATF-monitored jurisdiction. Sanctions screening must include direct, indirect, subsidiary, and consolidated ownership layers and must be repeated prior to board approval, before notarial execution, and at the opening of any Spanish bank account.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – Certificado de denominación social; online application via https://www.rmc.es / Sede Electrónica del Ministerio de Justicia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be submitted in Spanish or in another language using Latin characters. Non-Latin scripts must be fully transliterated into the Spanish/Latin alphabet, preserving accents (í, ó, á, é, ú, ñ) if applicable. The RMC issues the certificate based on the exact transliteration; the notarial deed and all public registries will reflect that exact spelling.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Denominations identical or phonetically/graphically equivalent to an existing registered Spanish or EU company (art. 404 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital)
State or public-institution terms requiring prior authorization, including 'Estado', 'Gobierno', 'Administración', 'Consejo', 'Nacional', 'Banco de España', 'Instituto Nacional'
Royal or institutional terms, including 'Real', 'Municipal', 'Central', 'Autonómico', absent ministerial or administrative approval
Misleading regulated-sector terms such as 'Banco', 'Seguros', 'Financiera', 'Asesoría Financiera', 'Fondo de Inversión', unless the entity holds or obtains the corresponding statutory license
Words or expressions contrary to law, public order, morality, or that would mislead the public
Foreign terms that cannot be transliterated into Latin script or are phonetically unacceptable in the Spanish legal-commercial register
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RMC rejects a proposed name, the applicant may: (i) download and review the official rejection grounds; (ii) submit a new application with up to three alternative proposed names at any time; (iii) file an administrative appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of service, attaching the rejection certificate and any supporting legal arguments; (iv) if the name was refused after notarial execution, request correction or substitution of the corporate name through a supplemental public deed and re-application before the Mercantile Registry. In practice, refiling with a materially different denominative string is faster and more cost-effective than an appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible: a virtual office or registered-address service can satisfy the formal domicile requirement of article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital at the pre-incorporation stage. However, for an AdTech/SSP/DSP platform, the Spanish registered office must correspond to a location where administration, correspondence, and accounting records can be effectively requested. A bare virtual office with no operational substance, management, or local personnel may attract AEAT, SEPBLAC, or commercial-registry scrutiny and may be rejected for banking or KYC purposes. Virtual office is therefore permissible but not advisable as the sole Spanish substance indicator.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate: approximately 10–15% within the first three post-incorporation years for newly registered digital-services limited companies. Unannounced inspections may be initiated by the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) under the general fraud-control framework, by SEPBLAC for AML compliance, and by the Registro Mercantil for concordance of registered office and actual management.

incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Upon formation of the Company, the initial Board of Directors resolves unanimously: To subscribe the initial share capital in the amounts and proportions detailed in the Articles of Association; To establish the registered office at the address specified therein; To appoint [Director Name] as Managing Director and [Director Name] as Secretary; To approve the execution of the public deed of incorporation and authorize the filing thereof with the Central Mercantile Registry within the legal term. The Board further authorizes the officers to perform all acts necessary for the registration, tax identification, and commencement of operations. This resolution is adopted in accordance with the provisions of the Articles of Association and the Companies Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Pre-incorporation: obtain the negative name certificate from the Registro Mercantil Central; execute the public deed before a notary. 2) Apply for the provisional tax identification number via Form 036 and deposit it at the competent AEAT office; the provisional NIF is assigned at notarization. 3) Register the SL in the Mercantile Registry and apply for the definitive NIF (CIF) using Form 036/037; the definitive NIF serves as the Spanish VAT identification number (e.g., B-12345678, preceded by 'ES' in intra-Community documents). 4) For intra-Community supplies, activate VIES and file recapitulative statements. 5) For a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment that makes taxable supplies in Spain: register for a non-resident NIF (key 'W') using Form 036, in principle through an appointed tax representative; an EU-established supplier may instead use the Union One-Stop-Shop for distance sales and electronically supplied services where the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold is not exceeded. 6) A fiscal representative may be mandatory for non-EU tax residents liable for VAT in Spain.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Spain; an SL is mandatorily a corporate taxpayer under Law 27/2014 (LIS). Relevant elections and mechanisms: (i) consolidated corporate income tax group election (arts. 58-70 LIS) where a parent holds, directly or indirectly, at least 75% of subsidiaries' share capital, declared via Form 036 before the relevant tax period; (ii) reduced CIT rate of 23% on the first EUR 50,000 of taxable base and 25% on the excess for micro-enterprises with net turnover below EUR 1,000,000 in the preceding tax period (art. 29.1 LIS, as amended by RDL 4/2024) - automatic, no election; (iii) optional 15% CIT rate for certified innovative startups under Law 28/2022, subject to a certificate from the competent authority; (iv) election for the ETVE regime for qualifying foreign securities holding entities; (v) within the hybrid-mismatch framework (Law 11/2021 implementing EU ATAD 1 and 2), elections and notional treatment may be applied to foreign permanent establishments and hybrid instruments as defined in arts. 22-23 LIS; an SL cannot elect pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Spain applies no general domestic VAT registration threshold; any taxable person habitually supplying taxable goods or services in Spain must register with AEAT from the first taxable transaction. The only statutorily relevant threshold is EUR 10,000 per calendar year for intra-EU distance sales of goods and electronically supplied services to final consumers (Union OSS threshold). Non-established foreign suppliers have no de minimis registration exemption for supplies taxed in Spain.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B electronic invoicing and billing-system certification are phased in under Ley 18/2022 (Ley Crea y Crece) and Real Decreto 1007/2023 (Verifactu). Verifactu requires billing software to generate verifiable invoices with a machine-readable JSON structure, a QR code, an encrypted hash-chain (hash encadenado), and a tamper-evident chronological log that must be retained and made immediately available to AEAT upon request; software producers must be certified. No universal continuous real-time fiscal clearance gateway applies; however, large taxpayers (turnover above EUR 6,000,000), VAT groups, and businesses applying the monthly VAT refund procedure must submit real-time VAT ledgers under SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) within 4 business days for issued invoices and 5 business days for received invoices. B2B e-invoicing is being introduced pursuant to the EU Council decision granting Spain a derogation from Article 218 of the EU VAT Directive, with phased application until 2028, using an interoperable AEAT public platform. Penalties: fixed fines up to EUR 10,000 per infringement for non-compliant billing software and invoicing offences under arts. 201-202 LGT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: Art. 21 LIVA zero-rates exports of tangible goods physically removed from the EU customs territory to a non-EU destination, provided the goods are dispatched or transported by the seller or on the seller's behalf and the export is evidenced by the Single Administrative Document (DUA/SAD) bearing the MRN and by a transport document confirming EU exit. Intra-Community supplies to a VAT-registered business customer are exempt with credit under Art. 25 LIVA, subject to the customer's valid EU VAT number, commercial documentation, and timely VIES recapitulative statement. Services: programmatic ad exchange, DSP, and SSP services (ISIC 7310) are not goods exports requiring zero-rating; the B2B place-of-supply rule (Art. 69.1 LIVA) situates the supply at the customer's establishment, so services to Spanish business customers carry 21% Spanish VAT, services to EU business customers are reverse-charged in the customer's Member State, and services to non-EU business customers are outside the scope of Spanish VAT. B2C electronically supplied services are deemed supplied where the consumer resides (Art. 69.2 LIVA) and may be declared through the Union OSS; substantiation of customer status and establishment remains required for all B2B cross-border services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo / Single Administrative Document) with MRN (Movement Reference Number) and AEAT exit validation
Transport document proving physical departure from the EU customs territory (Bill of Lading, CMR, or Air Waybill) issued in the exporter's name
Inward Remittance Certificate or banking evidence showing receipt of the export proceeds within 180 days, matching invoice currency and amount
Commercial invoice stating the applicable exemption provision (art. 21 or art. 25 LIVA) and, for intra-EU supplies, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number

For services outside the scope: contract, service order, evidence of the customer's business establishment (tax registration certificate or fiscal residency certificate), and digital or accounting records supporting the place of supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may reassess a zero-rated, exempt, or non-subjected transaction within the four-year limitation period where the documentary chain is incomplete, assessing 21% VAT plus late-payment interest. False, inaccurate, or missing export documentation triggers penalties under arts. 191-193 LGT of 50%-150% of the amount improperly excluded, aggravated in cases of concealment or false data. Invoicing, books, and records infractions (arts. 201-202 LGT and Ley Crea y Crece) attract fixed fines up to EUR 6,000 and proportional fines of 2% of invoice amounts; customs declaration violations under the LGT customs sanctioning regime may add penalties of 75%-150% of the customs value or tax at stake. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days without valid justification leads to immediate assessment, interest, and potential penalties under the anti-money-laundering regime (Law 10/2010). Organized or repeated abuse of export zero-rating, including missing-trader intra-Community fraud, exposes responsible directors to criminal liability under art. 305 of the Criminal Code where the aggregate defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, with imprisonment of 1-4 years, extended to 2-6 years where the amount exceeds EUR 600,000 or shell companies or organized structures are used; proportionality standards consistent with CJEU case law (e.g., Case C-884/19 Vădan) limit penalties for merely formal omissions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain); foreign investment and exchange control policy is jointly administered with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation and the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOM) within the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism; anti-money-laundering supervision is performed by SEPBLAC under the Banco de España umbrella.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a euro-area member with fully liberalized capital and current account convertibility under Articles 63-66 TFEU, Law 19/2003 on capital movements, and Royal Decree 1816/1991 on foreign transactions. Non-resident shareholders may freely invest in and capitalize an S.L., and may repatriate dividends, branch profits, loan repayments, liquidation proceeds, and capital gains without prior exchange-control authorization. Only ex post statistical declarations to the Banco de España and DGCOM are required for foreign investment monitoring and the Balance of Payments. Defensive FDI screening exists only for sectors implicating public order, national security, or regulated activities, and does not apply to ISIC 7310 programmatic AdTech supply-side platforms. Profit remittance is unrestricted subject to completion of corporate income tax obligations, audited financial statements, and withholding tax formalities; dividends paid to non-resident EU corporate shareholders may be exempt under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, and non-EU shareholders may rely on bilateral tax treaties to reduce the domestic 19% dividend withholding rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Spain does not impose mandatory surrender, conversion, or repatriation deadlines on export proceeds. A Spanish S.L., including a cross-border advertising and software service exporter under ISIC 7310, may retain 100% of its invoiced proceeds in EUR or foreign currency in Spanish credit institutions without conversion obligation. Invoicing, settlement, and reinvestment of such proceeds are free of exchange-control restrictions; only standard statistical reporting to the Banco de España applies, and all cross-border payments must be identified by the applicable BPM6-compliant transaction purpose code.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account in EUR with multi-currency and SWIFT/SEPA capabilities; Capital Escrow Account can be opened as a designated sub-account for share subscription funds pending corporate registration.

Operational Account in EUR with cross-border payment desk and commercial trade finance module; Capital Escrow Account available for temporary holding of capital contributions and proof of capital payment to the notary.

Operational Account in EUR and foreign currency clearing via its international desk; Capital Escrow Account feasible, but non-resident ownership requires a full AML documentation bundle before activation.
Operational Account in EUR with multi-currency capability and SWIFT gateways; suitable for low-risk AdTech treasury but requires a strong local or video-backed corporate compliance interview.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditional_Medium. An S.L. may use an EU-licensed electronic money institution or payment institution passporting into Spain under Directive (EU) 2015/2366 (PSD2) and Law 16/2009, provided the EMI is authorized in its home EEA state and has registered with the Banco de España if operating in Spain. Non-EU offshore digital EMIs without an EEA license cannot legally provide a primary treasury account to the Spanish S.L., cannot hold a Spanish IBAN, and are treated as incompatible with capital subscription and foreign-investment declarations. Approved EU EMIs are acceptable for low-value, high-frequency AdTech commission settlement and vendor payouts, but should be maintained only as secondary clearing rails; the primary treasury spine must be a Tier-1 Spanish bank account to preserve statutory reporting, notary interactions, and corporate-tax traceability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal Spanish statutory requirement that the directors or UBOs physically appear at the bank or notary when forming or banking an S.L.; formation may be completed through a notarial power of attorney, and Spanish banks accept remote identification via video and advanced electronic signature. However, practical Tier-1 bank onboarding for a newly incorporated S.L. owned by non-EU persons almost invariably requires at least one director/UBO to complete a video or in-person interview before the account is activated. Treasury planning must prepare apostilled and sworn-translated identification documents, certified incorporation documents, a board resolution authorizing account opening, proof of registered office, UBO declarations, source of wealth/funds evidence, and a business plan describing the programmatic advertising and SSP platform. A fully document-only, zero-interview onboarding is not realistic for non-resident-owned structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO obfuscation and complex multi-tier non-resident shareholding, including a parent holding company without visible substance or economic footprint in its home domicile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership chain chart to natural persons; certificate of good standing and registered agent certificate from the foreign registry; notarized and apostilled statutory accounts and annual returns; notarial power of attorney and certified board resolution for account opening; UBO declaration under Law 10/2010; employment contracts and professional footprint of decision-makers; explanation of the commercial rationale for the holding structure; commitment to provide audited accounts and annual bank reviews.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Programmatic AdTech revenue flows comprising high-volume, cross-border micro-payments from numerous DSP, SSP, and publisher counterparties, which can resemble money-laundering layering or transaction splitting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts with each material ad-exchange counterparty; platform dashboard screenshots showing deal-level transaction trails; invoices and credit notes matching every cleared payment; a cash-flow and revenue-flow narrative covering demand-side and supply-side settlement; segregation of platform commissions from client funds and media-buying pass-through funds; annual anti-money-laundering policy; and a forensic accounting report mapping settlement flows to contractual rights and obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous corporate object and sector inconsistency: the S.L. deed contains a broad or generic corporate purpose that does not expressly evidence an AdTech SSP/Ad-Exchange activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed drafted with a precise corporate object referencing ISIC 7310 and the operation of programmatic real-time bidding, advertising exchanges, and supply-side platforms; published website and product white-paper; technology licensing and hosting agreements; proof of domain and platform ownership; GDPR and data-processing agreements; professional indemnity insurance; and a company classification certificate showing NAICS 541810 or ISIC 7310 as the primary activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty or traffic-source risk from Latin American or other high-risk jurisdictions, including countries subject to FATF monitoring or Spanish national risk assessments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty AML/KYC questionnaires; IP-geo-blocking policy and list of blocked jurisdictions; sanctions, PEP, and watchlist screening procedures; contractual representations against terrorist financing and fraud; independent ad verification and anti-fraud vendor reports; traffic-quality audit evidence; and bank references from any prior payment institutions or EMIs through which advertising inventory or programmatic spend has flowed.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or parent-loan capital must be remitted through SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the S.L.'s Spanish IBAN account at a Tier-1 bank. The wire instruction must identify the beneficiary as the exact S.L. name with NIF, account IBAN, and BIC, and must state a payment purpose classified as foreign direct investment in equity or subordinated shareholder loan under the Spanish Balance of Payments and OECD FDI Benchmark Definition; banks require that the remitter name match the declared shareholder. For equity injections used during incorporation or a capital increase, the funds should first be credited to a temporary capital escrow account at the Spanish bank, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate, before the notary executes the escritura de constitucion or aumento de capital; after registration in the Mercantile Registry, the funds are transferred to the operational account. Foreign investment declaration to the DGCOM through the dedicated electronic portal must be filed within one month after the operation or registration, and additional transparency thresholds apply to investments above EUR 3,000,000 or from non-EU investors in critical sectors; no pre-approval is required for the present AdTech SSP scope. Supporting documentation includes the notarial deed, proof of account credit, bank statement, balance of payments purpose code, and the shareholder's identity and tax residence certificate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Euro-denominated payments to SEPA beneficiaries must be made via SEPA Credit Transfer using XML pain.001 files with IBAN-only routing, no correspondent fees, and attractive same-day processing. For payments to non-EEA counterparties, including Latin American media partners, DSPs, publishers, or infrastructure providers, the standard rail is SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer via the Spanish bank's international desk, with complete field 77B regulatory information, field 72 instructions for charges and exception handling, and the relevant payment narrative tied to service invoices. Commercial letters of credit may be used only where the counterparty is engaged in trade in physical goods or in clearly documented services requiring a documentary credit; such L/Cs must be issued under UCP600 and confirmed by a prime EEA correspondent bank. For typical AdTech software and advertising inventory settlement, documentary L/Cs are unnecessary and inefficient; outbound disbursements should be executed through SEPA CT or MT103, accompanied by a signed contract, invoice, tax certificate, and clearing evidence retained for Spanish corporate income tax and bank AML monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX purchases and sales at prevailing market rates, which are balance-sheet revaluation transactions rather than derivative contracts.
Outright FX forwards against EUR for major currencies, particularly USD and LatAm currencies, used to hedge forecast advertising revenue or media-purchase exposure.
FX swaps and forward-forward swaps for intraday and short-term liquidity matching between the S.L.'s EUR operating cash and USD settlement cash.
Cross-currency swaps for longer-term alignment of non-EUR denominated shareholder loans or intercompany payables with EUR functional-currency cash flows.
European-style FX options, including zero-cost collars, to protect against adverse FX movements while retaining upside on favorable revenue-side conversions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for currencies that lack a freely deliverable onshore forward market, such as certain restricted Latin American currencies, and only when the Spanish counterparty bank can prove physical settlement is impossible or legally prohibited in that jurisdiction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Cuentas Anuales) and Integrated Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil del domicilio social (Spanish Commercial Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved by the shareholders' meeting within 6 months after financial year-end and filed with the Commercial Registry within 1 month after approval. For a calendar-year SL: approve by 30 June and deposit by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers the 'cierre registral': the company's registry sheet is closed and no deeds, minutes, appointments, or charges may be registered until the overdue accounts are deposited. The closure is published in the Official Mercantile Gazette (BORME). Persistent non-filing may lead to appointment of a liquidator and eventual administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An SL must undergo a mandatory independent audit if, for two consecutive financial years, it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: total assets over €4,000,000; net turnover over €8,000,000; average headcount over 50 employees. Certain regulated sectors (credit, insurance, listed companies) are always subject to audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad - PGC), which is aligned with IFRS as adopted by the EU; consolidated financial statements are prepared under IFRS-EU for qualifying groups.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 10/2010, the SL must maintain an updated register of its ultimate beneficial owners. Each annual accounts deposit must include a UBO declaration to the Commercial Registry confirming current natural-person owners or stating that no change occurred. Share transfers recorded in the Register of Members must be reflected in this annual confirmation; omission renders the annual accounts filing incomplete.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)
Sole Shareholder Contracts Book (Libro de Contratos con el Socio Único), if applicable
